title: Decay verification so stale proof stops shipping
description: Verification is currently permanent and the proof that established it is not even retained (verifyBehavior accepts an evidence id but persists only behaviors.status). Repairs LB-22-PR-F1 with a canonical verification record and exact freshness formulas, LB-22-PR-F2 with an idempotent legacy migration and an executable decay-disabled rollback switch, and LB-22-PR-F3 with a backward-compatible ShipState contract that adds no new gate literal.

behaviors.title: Freshness derives deterministically from the canonical verification record
behaviors.trigger: substrate() derives freshness for a behavior whose verification record holds verified_at and an effective half-life
behaviors.expected: age_days = (clock_now - verified_at) / 86400; freshness is fresh when age_days < H, decaying when H <= age_days < 2H, and expired when age_days >= 2H, where H is the behavior's decay_half_life_days when set and the global default of 90 when null; H of 0 means never decays and always reads fresh
behaviors.verify: Against a disposable database with an injected clock, drive one verified behavior across the H and 2H boundaries and at the exact boundary instants, and read each expected band back through the real substrate surface

behaviors.title: Expired enforced behaviors hold shipping distinguishably, including mixed states
behaviors.trigger: review_ship_status evaluates enforced behaviors where at least one has expired verification, alone or mixed with never-verified and waived behaviors
behaviors.expected: Expired behaviors are classified unresolved, so the existing verification gate and hold disposition apply unchanged with no new gate literal; expired ids additionally appear in expired_behavior_ids, verification_expired_total counts them, verified_total counts only fresh and decaying verifications, waived behaviors remain resolved regardless of age, and the reason names the expired count separately from the never-verified count
behaviors.verify: Through the real review surface against a disposable database, evaluate an expired-only case and a mixed expired/never-verified/waived case, asserting gate, disposition, reason, verified_total, waived_total, verification_expired_total, unresolved_behavior_ids, and expired_behavior_ids in each

behaviors.title: Re-attestation replaces the verification record and restores shipping
behaviors.trigger: verifyBehavior runs again for an expired behavior with a new qualifying passing evidence id
behaviors.expected: verified_evidence_id and verified_at are replaced by that call's evidence and clock reading, freshness returns to fresh, and shipping recovers
behaviors.verify: Expire a behavior against a disposable database with an injected clock, re-verify it through the real verify surface with new evidence, and observe the replaced record, fresh band, and recovered shipping state

behaviors.title: Legacy migration preserves shipping, is idempotent, and rollback disables decay
behaviors.trigger: The additive migration runs against existing verified behaviors, including one whose most recent passing evidence is older than twice the effective half-life, and separately the decay-disabled switch is set
behaviors.expected: Every existing status='verified' behavior backfills verified_at to the single migration timestamp regardless of its evidence age, so no previously shipping behavior is converted to a hold by the rollout; verified_evidence_id backfills from the most recent passing evidence where one exists and is null otherwise; decay_half_life_days is left null for existing and new rows alike; only rows with a null verified_at are touched so re-running changes nothing; and setting the global half-life to 0 makes every behavior read fresh regardless of age
behaviors.verify: Seed a disposable database with representative legacy rows (verified with one passing evidence, verified with multiple evidence, verified with passing evidence older than 2H, verified with no evidence, verified with only failed evidence), record pre-migration shipping, run the migration twice asserting identical results, assert post-migration shipping is identical to pre-migration including for the aged-evidence row which must read fresh, then set the decay-disabled switch and assert every behavior still reads fresh

behaviors.title: The visualizer shows decay
behaviors.trigger: The visualizer renders a decaying or expired behavior node
behaviors.expected: The node shows a distinct tone and a freshness line
behaviors.verify: Render the node in web/src/graph.ts and observe the freshness tone and line

planning.outcome: Verification expires on a deterministic schedule and must be re-attested; stale proof cannot ship an enforced behavior, and the rollout preserves every previously shipping behavior by grandfathering legacy verifications to the migration timestamp.
planning.appetite: One freshness slice over a new canonical verification record, adding no new ShipState gate literal.
non_goals: Bitemporal valid_from/valid_to intervals and supersession edges (stay in Rordi)
Adding a new gate or disposition literal, which would fall through the prime.ts nextActionFor default and misreport next_action
Decaying advisory behaviors, waivers, or planning-review approvals

work_units.title: Persist the canonical verification record and derive freshness
work_units.done_when: verifyBehavior persists verified_evidence_id and verified_at, and substrate() derives the three bands by the exact formulas

work_units.title: Extend ShipState for expiration without a new gate literal
work_units.done_when: Expired behaviors hold at the existing verification gate with expired_behavior_ids, verification_expired_total, and a reason naming both counts

work_units.title: Idempotent legacy backfill and an executable decay-disabled switch
work_units.done_when: The migration is repeatable, grandfathers every legacy verification so pre-migration shipping is preserved including for aged evidence, and the global half-life of 0 disables decay

work_units.title: Render decay in the visualizer
work_units.done_when: Decaying and expired nodes are visually distinct

proofs.method: Injected clock across H and 2H boundaries and at exact boundary instants, read through the real substrate surface.
Expired-only and mixed expired/never-verified/waived cases through the real review surface, asserting all nine ShipState fields plus the two new ones.
Expire, re-verify through the real verify path with new evidence, observe replaced record and recovered shipping.

Representative legacy rows including one with passing evidence older than 2H, migrated twice for idempotence, asserting post-migration shipping equals pre-migration shipping, then the decay-disabled switch asserted to keep everything fresh.
Render a decaying and an expired node and observe tone and freshness line.

planning.production_wiring: Additive columns on behaviors in db.ts migrate(): verified_at TEXT null, verified_evidence_id TEXT null referencing evidence(id), decay_half_life_days INTEGER null. verifyBehavior in src/domain.ts (currently domain.ts:607-628, which persists only status) also writes verified_evidence_id from its existing validated evidenceId argument and verified_at from the domain clock. A single injectable clock is threaded into substrate() defaulting to the system clock so proofs can time-inject. The global default half-life is one constant, DECAY_HALF_LIFE_DEFAULT_DAYS = 90, overridable by the LOOPBREAKER_DECAY_HALF_LIFE_DAYS environment variable, where 0 disables decay entirely and is the rollback switch. substrate() computes freshness per enforced behavior and extends the shipping read model with expired_behavior_ids and verification_expired_total while leaving all nine existing ShipState fields and the five existing gate literals unchanged. web/src/graph.ts renders the freshness tone.
planning.rollback: Set LOOPBREAKER_DECAY_HALF_LIFE_DAYS=0. Every behavior then reads fresh regardless of age, expired_behavior_ids is empty, verification_expired_total is 0, and shipping evaluates exactly as it did before the change. The added columns remain but are inert, so no schema reversal and no data loss.
planning.migration: Additive nullable columns. Every existing status='verified' behavior backfills verified_at to the single migration timestamp, regardless of the age of its evidence. This grandfathering is deliberate: evidence.created_at records when the evidence row was created, not when verification occurred, and verifyBehavior persists no time today, so there is no reliable historical verification timestamp to honour. Using that approximation to revoke shipping status on upgrade would be overreach, so every behavior instead starts its clock at migration and decays honestly from there. verified_evidence_id backfills from the most recent passing evidence where one exists and is null otherwise. decay_half_life_days is left null for existing and new rows so both inherit the global default. The backfill touches only rows with a null verified_at, so it is idempotent and safe to re-run.

risks.risk: A too-short default half-life expires healthy work and creates churn.
risks.mitigation: Default 90 days, per-behavior override, and a global 0 switch that disables decay outright.

risks.risk: Backfilling verified_at from evidence age could silently convert shipping projects into holds.
risks.mitigation: Explicit grandfather policy: every legacy verified behavior backfills to the migration timestamp regardless of evidence age, and LB-22-B4 proves pre-migration shipping is preserved including for a row whose passing evidence is older than 2H.

risks.risk: A new gate or disposition literal would fall through prime.ts nextActionFor's default and report next_action ship for an unshippable issue.
risks.mitigation: Expiration reuses the existing verification gate and hold disposition; adding a literal is a named non-goal.
